title: UK CPI — November 2026 consumer price inflation (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), published INSIDE the MPC's final meeting day, hours before the December vote is taken
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationuknovember2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the ONS release page reads 'Consumer price inflation, UK: November 2026', 'Release date: 16 December 2026 7:00am', and 'This release is not yet published'. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics — the same gap uk-cpi-2026-09-16, uk-cpi-2026-10-21 and uk-cpi-2026-11-18 were filed under. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of boe-decision-2026-12-17 and of uk-cpi-2026-11-18, both 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding BOTH proposals for this id — proposals/uk-cpi-2026-12-16.from-boe-decision-2026-12-17.json and proposals/uk-cpi-2026-12-16.from-uk-cpi-2026-11-18.json — each read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md. Both proposals' placement finding stands and the initial research SHARPENS it from a gap into an overlap: the BoE's own minutes headers show the announcement day is the day AFTER the meeting ends (July 2026 minutes, fetched: 'meeting ending on 29 July 2026', published 30 July; and, verbatim, 'meeting ending on 16 September will be published on 17 September 2026'). A 17 December announcement therefore means a meeting ENDING 16 December — the morning this print publishes at 07:00. Verified in four of the last five Decembers (Nov-2021 CPI 15 Dec / meeting ending 15 Dec; Nov-2022 CPI 14 Dec / meeting ending 14 Dec; Nov-2024 CPI 18 Dec / meeting ending 18 Dec; Nov-2025 CPI 17 Dec / meeting ending 17 Dec; only Dec-2023 missed). The Dec-2025 instance is the precedent that gives this entry stakes: the MPC voted 5-4 to cut to 3.75% and its Monetary Policy Summary's first substantive sentence reads 'CPI inflation has fallen since the previous meeting, to 3.2%' — the number published 07:00 that same morning. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDS, AND IT REVERSES THE SIGN THE SIBLING LEDGERS IMPLY: this print's annual rate most likely RISES. Nov-2025 m/m was -0.215% (D7BT 139.8 -> 139.5), the second-softest November in thirteen years against a 13-year mean of +0.11%, and ONS named food and alcohol/tobacco as the two largest downward monthly contributions. Both are set to reverse. The 2026 Budget is 28 October (HM Treasury, per uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28) against 26 November in 2025, so the duty uprating lands in the NOVEMBER index rather than December: CPI division 02 (D7BV) rose +1.26%/+2.59%/+1.42% m/m in the late-October-Budget Novembers of 2018/2021/2024 and -0.45% in Nov-2025, worth about +0.07pp on the annual rate at the 2026 weight of 37.1650/1000. Food (D7BU) fell -0.209% in Nov-2025 against a 10-year November mean of +0.423%, worth about +0.045pp at 109.6059/1000. Energy adds ~+0.012pp of fixed-tariff drift with no cap step inside the Oct-Dec cap quarter. Attributable push +0.11 to +0.19pp; full reversion to the November norm would be +0.33pp. THE ATTRIBUTION RULE: a higher 16 December headline is duty timing plus an easy base, NOT reacceleration — services (D7NN) fell 4.4% to 3.4% across 2026 and core (DKO8) 3.2% to 2.6%, and services carries no VAT, duty or cap distortion at all. Tiered LOW to match the sibling UK CPI entries: symbols: [], no rates- or sterling-keyed house playbook, and this calendar's whole symbol universe is eight US mega-caps. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action. Ledger: docs/research/events/uk-cpi-2026-12-16.md
